summary: Closed the silent partition row-loss defect reproduced by the 2026-09-18 reference run. The writer now refuses (fail-closed) any incoming batch whose EventKeys are not already recorded in the existing on-disk Parquet file, raising a new :class:`SilentRowLossError` with the offending EventKey set; the runner maps that to a ``partition_row_loss_guard`` reason code and halts the run with ``complete=False``. The planner now aligns collection interval boundaries to the partition grid whenever ``max_blocks_per_sub_range`` is a multiple of ``blocks_per_partition`` (the production default of 10 000 / 100 is a multiple, so grid alignment is the default), prepending a short pre-window for the partial first cell so the pool's Initialize event is preserved. A new ``storage.reconciliation`` module compares every partition's ``event_index`` EventKey set against the rows the on-disk Parquet file carries; the data-quality verifier accepts the reconciliation reports and forces ``complete=false`` with the new ``partition_event_index_parquet_mismatch`` reason code while any partition disagrees. Re-checking the real ``/home/lpdev/lp-data`` dataset through the new reconciliation path surfaces exactly the two missing Swap partitions the contract names (``range=55586200-55586299`` and ``range=55726200-55726299``), each with one EventKey missing from the Parquet file. The 2026-09-18 dataset is left untouched; this task records the observation as evidence and does not repair the bytes. Re-run idempotency remains intact (T031 contract re-stated) — repeated writes of the same batch are silently skipped without triggering the guard.

residual_risks: The 2026-09-18 reference dataset is left untouched per the T037 Must-not clause (no repair of the two lost Swap rows). Downstream tasks that depend on a complete dataset must run the new reconciliation check first; ``complete=true`` now requires every partition's event_index set to match the Parquet file.
